verdict_reason: I lift the prior YELLOW. The paper's Eq. 9 does say exactly this -- I pulled arXiv:2503.13530v1 and read Definition 2 verbatim: lambda_{m,n}(X_m) = lim_{|delta_m| -> 0} (1/(n-m)) ln(|delta_{m,n}| / |delta_m|), with X_0 the input embedding and X_m the m-th block's output, so n-m is the number of blocks traversed. BLME perturbs at the embedding (m = 0) and its kept profile is [emb, b_0 ... b_{L-2}], so the last point is X_{L-1} and n - m = L - 1, which is exactly the _meta_n_transitions the code divides by (verified: 5 for the 6-layer models, 11 for the 12-layer, 23 for gpt2-medium). growth_rate_per_block therefore IS Eq. 9. Closed-form check on linear stacks d_l = d_0 a^l: at L = 2/6/12/24/36 it returns 0.139773/0.139763/0.139762/0.139762/0.139762 against ln(1.15) = 0.139762, -0.223137/-0.223145/-0.223143/-0.223143/-0.223144 against ln(0.8) = -0.223144, and 0.693147/0.693148/0.693148/0.693147/0.693147 against ln(2) = 0.693147 -- exact to 1e-6, with the 1.1e-5 outlier only at L = 2 where a single transition carries the finite-epsilon noise. I also REFUTE the redundancy hypothesis: growth_slope is not depth-invariant, it is the OPPOSITE. Fitting log d against depth normalised to [0,1] multiplies the per-block exponent by (L-1), and on the same fixed gain a = 1.15 the slope reads 0.139773/0.698818/1.537385/3.214527/4.891668 at L = 2/6/12/24/36 -- exactly (L-1) ln a. On real models the two are not even proxies for each other: over distilgpt2/gpt2/pythia-70m/pythia-160m/gpt2-medium, pearson(growth_slope, growth_log_ratio) = 0.103, because the measured log-divergence profile is far from linear. The new key is not redundant; it is the only depth-free one.
comparable_reason: None of the three exported scalars is a clean cross-model quantity, and the new one is the most depth-locked. Measured on 5 models (fp32, 10 default probe sentences, rel_eps 1e-3, seed 42): growth_rate_per_block = 0.4303 (distilgpt2, 6L), 0.5891 (pythia-70m, 6L), 0.2511 (gpt2, 12L), 0.2762 (pythia-160m, 12L), 0.1463 (gpt2-medium, 24L), Spearman -0.949 with n_layers -- consistent with the -0.964 measured earlier over 8 models. The reason is arithmetic and worth stating: the TOTAL log-amplification growth_log_ratio is roughly depth-invariant on real models (2.1516 / 2.9457 / 2.7616 / 3.0377 / 3.3644, rho +0.738), so dividing it by (L-1) INJECTS a 1/(L-1) depth dependence rather than removing one. growth_slope carries the opposite factor ((L-1) x the per-block rate) and lands at rho -0.211 here and -0.581 over the earlier 8-model set -- a partial cancellation between two depth terms, not a depth-free number.
github_reason: Li, Leng, Ding, Mo, Yang 2025 (arXiv:2503.13530) links no repository. I re-pulled the abstract page and the full v1 PDF (17 pages, 1.4 MB) and searched the extracted text for 'github', 'http', 'available at', 'repository', 'code' and 'data availability': no footnote URL, no arXiv Code link, and a targeted GitHub search for the title/authors/arXiv id finds nothing. BLME's own metadata marks the task proxy-only. There is genuinely nothing to cross-run.
paper_reason: Li et al. publish no QLE table. The quasi-Lyapunov exponent appears only as a heatmap (Fig. 6) on an unnamed 'LLaMa-based' checkpoint with the input 'Cats are animals', with no axis values and no released script. The only numbers in the paper are an output-decomposition split (55.77% mlp / 44.23% attn / 0.0009% initial input) and a CMMLU robustness result, neither a QLE. What the paper DOES pin down and I verified against the code: Eq. 9 carries the 1/(n-m) normalisation, and Eq. 10 -- the form the authors say they actually use -- defines the perturbation RELATIVELY as delta'_m = k X_m, which is what BLME does (rel_eps * ||h_token|| per token).
confounds_reason: The depth factor in growth_slope is arithmetic, not statistical: I confirmed on synthetic linear stacks that the SAME per-block gain gives slope 0.1398 / 0.6988 / 1.5374 / 3.2145 / 4.8917 at 2 / 6 / 12 / 24 / 36 blocks, i.e. exactly (L-1) ln a. Empirically over 5 models: growth_slope rho -0.211 with n_layers, growth_log_ratio +0.738, growth_rate_per_block -0.949 (and -0.964 / -0.970 vs n_layers / d_model over the earlier 8-model set). Separately, perturbation_growth_per_layer[0] is exactly 0.0 by construction on every model (it is log(d_0/d_0)), so any .min aggregation of that list is a hard constant.
defects: CODE: the final block is still never measured. Unlike dynamics_coe -- which was fixed in the same round by hooking layers[-1] to recover the raw deepest-block output -- this task still uses the blunt block_output_count(model) trim, so the profile keeps [emb, b_0 ... b_{L-2}] and stops one block short. Verified: nprofile = n_layers exactly on distilgpt2 (6), gpt2 (12), pythia-70m (6), pythia-160m (12), gpt2-medium (24), i.e. pythia-70m reports 5 of its 6 blocks. The same forward hook that fixed coe.py applies verbatim here and would make n - m = L.

RE-RUN REQUIRED: growth_rate_per_block is a new key absent from every archived result, and the post-final-norm trim (correct, but value-changing: mean |42%| change in growth_log_ratio, up to -68.6% on gpt2-large) already invalidated the stored values.

CODE: growth_slope and growth_log_ratio are near-duplicates whenever the profile is close to linear (identical to 6 decimals on synthetic stacks) but nearly independent on real models (pearson 0.103 over 5 models), so which of the two a downstream regression picks up is set by profile curvature, not by anything the metric names.
CODE: rel_eps (0.001) and n_samples_used (10) are returned without a _meta_ prefix, so they enter the feature matrix as zero-variance columns. _meta_n_transitions is correctly prefixed.
CODE: perturbation_growth_per_layer[0] is identically 0.0 on every model.
CODE: one random perturbation direction and one finite epsilon, with no eps -> 0 linearity check and no direction ensemble, so this is a secant sensitivity rather than the limit Eq. 9 defines.

CODE: the perturbation is built and added in the model's dtype (noise.to(dtype=E.dtype)), so on a bf16 zoo a large fraction of the requested per-coordinate changes round to zero before the forward pass. Generate and add in fp32.
fix: Promote growth_rate_per_block to the primary scalar and either drop growth_slope or replace it with slope/(L-1), so the two exported numbers are not one depth-multiplied and one depth-divided version of the same thing. Replace the block_output_count trim with the layers[-1] forward hook already used in coe.py, so n - m = L and the deepest block is measured. Prefix rel_eps and n_samples_used with _meta_. Sweep at least three decreasing rel_eps values and several directions and report the spread, so the quantity is a limit rather than one secant. Build and add the perturbation in fp32 regardless of model dtype. Mark every archived value stale.
